stem:
Gwanda Quarries Ltd, a company with a quarry near Gwanda, has the following equity at the start of its financial year, 1 January 2026.

| Item | US\$ |
| --- | ---: |
| Ordinary shares of US\$1 each, fully paid | 440,000 |
| Share premium | 56,000 |
| General reserve | 64,000 |
| Retained earnings | 172,000 |
| **Total equity** | 732,000 |

**1 March 2026.** The company issued 120,000 new ordinary shares of US\$1 at US\$1.45, payable US\$0.55 on application and US\$0.90 on allotment (including the premium). Applications were received for 156,000 shares. The directors allotted 120,000 shares and refunded the applicants for the other 36,000 shares. All the allotment money was received.

**1 July 2026.** The company made a bonus issue of one new share for every eight shares then in issue. The general reserve was used first, and the balance was taken from the share premium account.

Ignore the profit for the year and any dividends.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: For the issue on 1 March 2026, calculate:

parts.label: (i)
parts.stem: the application money received
parts.explanation: 156,000 × US\$0.55 = US\$85,800; every applicant pays with the application.
parts.workedSolution: 1. 156,000 × US\$0.55 = US\$85,800; every applicant pays with the application.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.stem: the refund to the unsuccessful applicants

parts.label: (iii)
parts.stem: the share premium credited

parts.label: (iv)
parts.stem: the net cash received from the issue
parts.explanation: Application money kept 66,000 + allotment money 108,000 = US\$174,000 (= 120,000 × US\$1.45).
parts.workedSolution: 1. Application money kept 66,000 + allotment money 108,000 = US\$174,000 (= 120,000 × US\$1.45).

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Prepare the application and allotment account.

points.description: Debit: ordinary share capital 120,000 and share premium 54,000 on allotment (total 174,000)
Both sides total 193,800 so the account balances

answerSpec.modelAnswer:
**Application and allotment account**

| Date | Details | US\$ | Date | Details | US\$ |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- | --- | ---: |
| 1 Mar | Bank (refund) | 19,800 | 1 Mar | Bank (application money) | 85,800 |
| 1 Mar | Ordinary share capital | 120,000 | 1 Mar | Bank (allotment money) | 108,000 |
| 1 Mar | Share premium | 54,000 |  |  |  |
|  |  | **193,800** |  |  | **193,800** |

parts.explanation: One mark for each group of entries and one for the balance.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: For the bonus issue on 1 July 2026, calculate:

parts.label: (i)
parts.stem: the number of bonus shares issued

parts.label: (ii)
parts.stem: the amount taken from the share premium account
parts.explanation: Total capitalised = 70,000 × US\$1 = US\$70,000; general reserve 64,000 is used first, so the share premium provides 70,000 - 64,000 = US\$6,000.
parts.workedSolution: 1. Total capitalised = 70,000 × US\$1 = US\$70,000; general reserve 64,000 is used first, so the share premium provides 70,000 - 64,000 = US\$6,000.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Calculate, at the end of the financial year (ignoring profit and dividends):

parts.label: (i)
parts.stem: the issued ordinary share capital

parts.label: (ii)
parts.stem: total equity
parts.explanation: 732,000 + net cash from the issue 174,000 = US\$906,000; the bonus issue does not change total equity.
parts.workedSolution: 1. 732,000 + net cash from the issue 174,000 = US\$906,000; the bonus issue does not change total equity.

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: Explain why the bonus issue does not change total equity, although the market price of each share is expected to fall.

points.description: A bonus issue only transfers amounts from reserves to share capital within equity, and no cash is received
The number of shares increases while the total value of the company is unchanged
So the value of each share, and the market price per share, falls in proportion

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The bonus issue converts reserves into share capital, so equity moves from one part to another and no cash is received. There are more shares sharing the same value, so each share is worth less.

parts.explanation: One mark for each of the three points.

explanation: This ZIMSEC Paper 2 style question combines an oversubscribed share issue, the application and allotment account and a bonus issue.
hints: Application money is received from all applicants.
The bonus is based on the shares in issue after 1 March.

stem:
Chitungwiza Furniture Ltd makes beds and cupboards for schools and hostels. Extracts from its financial statements for the years 2024 and 2025 are given below. Use year-end figures. Give percentages to one decimal place, ratios as x : 1 to two decimal places and days to the nearest whole day. For return on equity use profit for the year divided by equity.

| Item | 2024 US\$ | 2025 US\$ |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Revenue | 572,000 | 618,000 |
| of which credit sales | 514,800 | 556,200 |
| Cost of sales | 371,800 | 438,780 |
| Profit from operations | 91,200 | 60,020 |
| Finance costs | 5,400 | 11,800 |
| Profit for the year | 68,100 | 36,520 |
| Inventory | 57,300 | 88,400 |
| Trade receivables | 66,800 | 97,100 |
| Cash and cash equivalents | 35,200 | 7,300 |
| Trade payables and other current liabilities | 61,600 | 94,000 |
| Loan notes (non-current) | 63,000 | 127,000 |
| Equity (shares and reserves) | 344,700 | 356,800 |
| Capital employed | 407,700 | 483,800 |

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Calculate the gross profit margin for:

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Calculate return on capital employed for:

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Calculate the current ratio for:

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Calculate the acid test ratio for:

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: Calculate trade receivables days for:

parts.label: (f)
parts.stem: Calculate return on equity for:

parts.label: (g)
parts.stem: Comment on the profitability of the company in 2025 compared with 2024.

points.description: The gross profit margin fell from 35.0% to 29.0%, although revenue rose
ROCE fell from 22.4% to 12.4% and return on equity from 19.8% to 10.2%
Possible causes: lower selling prices or dearer materials, and higher finance costs and a bigger capital base from the extra loan

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Profitability has fallen. The gross margin dropped to 29.0% and ROCE and return on equity are both lower, probably because of price cuts or dearer materials, and because the extra loan has increased capital employed and finance costs without matching profit.

parts.explanation: One mark each for the margin, the two returns and a cause.

parts.label: (h)
parts.stem: Comment on the liquidity and the control of working capital in 2025.

points.description: The current ratio fell from 2.59 to 2.05 and the acid test from 1.66 to 1.11
Receivables days rose from 47 to 64: customers take longer to pay
Cash fell to US\$7,300 while inventory rose to US\$88,400

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Liquidity has weakened: both ratios fell, cash is very low and inventory has grown. Customers also take longer to pay, so working capital is absorbing cash.

parts.explanation: One mark each for the ratios, receivables and cash or inventory.

parts.label: (i)
parts.stem: The directors ask a bank for a further loan. Advise the bank, giving two reasons.

points.description: Profitability and liquidity have both weakened, and gearing has risen with the previous loan
Interest cover is falling because finance costs have doubled; a further loan adds to the risk
Recommendation: decline or lend only with security and a plan to restore the margin and collect receivables

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The bank should be cautious: profit, ROCE and liquidity have all fallen and the finance costs are already high. It should lend only with security and a plan for a better margin and faster collection.

parts.explanation: One mark for the weakness, one for the interest burden and one for a recommendation.

explanation: This ZIMSEC Paper 2 style question asks for profitability, liquidity, efficiency and return on equity ratios and for comments and advice.
hints: Capital employed is given in the table.
For return on equity use the profit for the year.
